mcq.q: A firm's total revenue from selling 1, 2, 3 and 4 units is ₹20, ₹36, ₹48 and ₹56. The marginal revenue of the 3rd unit is:
mcq.explain: Marginal revenue is the addition to total revenue from selling one more unit: MR of the 3rd unit = TR(3) − TR(2) = 48 − 36 = ₹12. The value ₹48 is total revenue and ₹16 is average revenue at 3 units (48 ÷ 3). MR falls as more is sold, so the firm faces a downward-sloping demand curve.

mcq.q: A firm faces the demand curve P = 60 − 2Q. Its total revenue is maximum at an output of:
mcq.explain: Total revenue TR = P × Q = 60Q − 2Q². Marginal revenue MR = 60 − 4Q. Total revenue is maximum where MR = 0, that is 60 − 4Q = 0, giving Q = 15. At that output, price is 60 − 30 = ₹30 and total revenue is ₹450.

mcq.q: Average revenue is ₹30 and price elasticity of demand is 3. Marginal revenue is:
mcq.explain: The relationship is MR = AR × (1 − 1/e) = 30 × (1 − 1/3) = 30 × 2/3 = ₹20. When demand is elastic (e > 1), MR is positive; when e = 1, MR is zero; and when demand is inelastic, MR is negative.
mcq.topic: MR, AR and price elasticity of demand

mcq.q: When price elasticity of demand equals one, marginal revenue is:
mcq.explain: Using MR = AR (1 − 1/e), when e = 1, MR = AR × (1 − 1) = 0. This is the point where total revenue is at its maximum. When demand is elastic MR is positive, and when it is inelastic MR is negative, so a firm never chooses to produce in the inelastic range.
mcq.topic: MR, AR and price elasticity of demand

mcq.q: Under perfect competition, a firm sells every unit at the market price of ₹25. Its average revenue and marginal revenue are:
mcq.explain: A perfectly competitive firm is a price taker: it can sell any quantity at the ruling price. Each additional unit adds exactly ₹25 to total revenue, so MR = ₹25, and average revenue (TR ÷ Q) is also ₹25. The firm's demand curve is horizontal, with AR = MR = price.
mcq.fast: Perfect competition: P = AR = MR (horizontal line).

mcq.q: A market with many sellers selling differentiated products, with some selling costs and fairly easy entry, is:
mcq.explain: Monopolistic competition combines features of monopoly and competition: there are many sellers, but each sells a slightly differentiated product (brands of soap or toothpaste), spends on advertising and other selling costs, and has some control over its price. Entry and exit are relatively free.
mcq.fast: Many sellers + product differentiation + selling costs = monopolistic competition.

mcq.q: A market with only one buyer and many sellers is called:
mcq.explain: Monopsony is a market with a single buyer, for example a sole employer in a small town buying labour. Monopoly is a single seller, duopoly is two sellers, and oligopsony is a market with a few buyers. The buyer in a monopsony can influence the price it pays.
mcq.fast: Mono-psony = one buyer; mono-poly = one seller.

mcq.q: Markets classified as local, regional, national and international are classified on the basis of:
mcq.explain: Markets can be classified by area (local, regional, national, international), by time (very short period, short period, long period), by nature of transactions (spot and forward), by volume (wholesale and retail), by regulation (regulated and unregulated), and by type of competition. Local to international is the area basis.

mcq.q: A profit-maximising firm is in equilibrium where:
options: MR = MC, with MC rising at that output
mcq.explain: Profit is maximised where marginal revenue equals marginal cost, provided that MC is rising at that point, i.e. MC cuts MR from below. If MR > MC, producing more adds to profit; if MR < MC, producing less adds to profit. Maximum TR is a different goal, and AR = AC gives only normal profit.
mcq.fast: Profit max: MR = MC + MC cuts MR from below.

mcq.q: In the short run, a firm making losses should continue to produce as long as the price covers at least its:
mcq.explain: In the short run fixed costs must be paid whether or not the firm produces. If price at least covers average variable cost, producing reduces the loss by contributing something towards fixed costs. If price falls below AVC, the firm should shut down. Price must cover ATC only in the long run.
mcq.fast: Short run: shut down only if P < AVC.
